analysis.description: This paper explores new approaches to combining information encoded within learned representations of auto-encoders. It introduces models capable of combining attributes of multiple inputs that can fool an adversarial discriminator when synthesizing realistic outputs. The study focuses on semi-supervised learning by learning a mixing function to produce interpolations of latent representations. The formulation is examined through diverse mixup strategies, including continuous interpolations and genetically-inspired recombinations.

type.justification: The paper is primarily theoretical as it explores new methodologies for mixing latent representations in auto-encoders using adversarial training and discusses various potential mixup strategies and techniques.
type.quote: Therefore, in this paper we explore the use of such a mechanism in the context of auto-encoders through an exploration of various mixing functions.

name.justification: The research primarily centers around auto-encoders which are a key component of unsupervised learning frameworks.
name.quote: The auto-encoder is a fundamental building block in unsupervised learning.

name.justification: The paper applies its proposed methodologies in the context of semi-supervised learning, exploring the use of a mixing function consistent with class labels.
name.quote: Furthermore, we explore the use of such an architecture in the context of semi-supervised learning, where we learn a mixing function.

name.justification: The paper employs adversarial learning techniques to train models that can produce realistic outputs from mixed latent representations.
name.quote: We leverage adversarial learning (Goodfellow et al., 2014), where here we train a discriminator to distinguish between decoded mixed and real data points.

name.justification: AMR is the primary model discussed within the paper, where it introduces this new strategy for mixing latent codes using auto-encoders and adversarial training.
name.quote: With this in mind, we propose adversarial mixup resynthesis (AMR), where part of the auto-encoder’s objective is to produce mixes which, when decoded, are indistinguishable from real images.

is_contributed.justification: The model is a novel contribution introduced and thoroughly explored within this paper.

is_compared.quote: The results we present generally show there are benefits to mixing. In Table 1 we obtain the best results across SVHN, with k = 3 mixup performing the best.

name.justification: Manifold Mixup is discussed as a part of the mixing strategy that is used within AMR and its variations.
name.quote: Manifold mixup (Verma et al., 2018) implements mixing in the hidden space through convex combinations: Mix_mixup (h_1, h_2) = αh_1 + (1 − α)h_2, where α ∈ [0, 1] is sampled from a Uniform(0, 1) distribution.

is_contributed.justification: Manifold Mixup is an existing technique that the paper refers to and utilizes within their proposed framework.
is_contributed.quote: In Verma et al. (2018), these random convex combinations are computed in the hidden space of the network.

is_executed.justification: There is no specific mention in the paper of Manifold Mixup being executed as part of the experiments, rather it's referenced as a technique related to the proposed strategy.
is_executed.quote: Manifold Mixup is discussed as part of the context and surrounding techniques explored in implementing adversarial mixup resynthesis.

is_compared.justification: It is discussed as a conceptual basis rather than being compared as a separate model.
